title: Protocol to characterize the melanoma tumor immune microenvironment in mice from single cell to flow cytometry analysis
protocol: Seed tumoral cells into 100 mm culture dishes.
Grow the seeded cells until they reach 90% confluence at 37°C and 5% CO2 in appropriate culture medium.
Remove the medium from the culture dish by gentle aspiration.
Wash the cells twice with sterile 1× PBS.
Add trypsin-EDTA to completely cover the cells, using approximately 1 mL.
Incubate the cells at 37°C for 2 minutes.
Check under the microscope if the cells have detached from the plate.
After incubation, add 4 mL of complete medium to stop the trypsin reaction and collect all liquid in a sterile tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 5 minutes at 400–600 g at room temperature.
Remove the trypsin solution by aspiration.
Resuspend the cells with fresh medium containing serum, typically using about 1 mL of medium.
Determine the concentration of cells using a hemocytometer or Burker camera.
Wash cells with sterile 1× PBS.
Add 1× PBS to the tube and spin down cells at 400–600 g for 5 min.
Aspirate PBS from the tube.
Resuspend cells in fresh PBS to a concentration of 1 × 10^6 cells/100 μL.
Transfer cells to a sterile 1.5 mL tube.
Optional: Add an equal volume (μL) of thawed Matrigel to cells and mix carefully with pipette.
Critical: Thaw Matrigel on ice because it will solidify at room temperature.
Mix 100 μL of cells alone using an insulin syringe.
Or mix 200 μL of cell/Matrigel mixture using an insulin syringe.
Anesthetize mice using isoflurane.
Shave the skin working area on the left or right flank of the mice.
Inject cells into the shaved area of the mice.
Keep syringes with cells on ice to avoid polymerization of the Matrigel.
Measure tumor volume three times a week using calipers.
Determine tumor volume by measuring the greatest longitudinal diameter (length, D) and the greatest transverse diameter (width, d).
Calculate tumor size using the formula: Tumor weight (TW, mg) = (D × d²)/2 = mm³
Sacrifice mice using direct cardiac puncture without opening the thorax.
Collect blood from the sacrificed mice.
Obtain xenograft tumors for collection.
Collect bone marrow from the sacrificed mice.
Collect spleen organs from the sacrificed mice.
Practice taking blood directly from the visible heart, especially for smaller species.
Take blood as soon as possible after the animal's death to prevent coagulation.
Fix a 21G syringe needle and carefully remove its cover.
Expel air from the syringe.
Place the animal on its back in a horizontal position.
Clean the thoracic fur with ethanol.
Locate the thoracic cage and xiphoid process (lower part of the sternum).
Insert the needle under the xiphoid process at about 30 degrees to the left while pulling the plunger gently.
Continue pulling the plunger to aspirate blood without moving the needle once heart perforation is achieved.
Repeat the procedure if no blood appears in the needle.
Slowly withdraw and adjust the needle if the flow stops rapidly, indicating possible perforation on the back of the heart.
Release pressure on the plunger when enough blood is collected.
Withdraw the needle from the animal.
Slowly expel blood from the syringe into Heparin/EDTA tubes.
Dispose of the needle before expelling blood to avoid damaging blood cells.
Optional: Soak a syringe with heparin.
Transfer the blood to a 1.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge the tube to obtain plasma.
Place the animal ventral side up on a clean dissection board.
Clean the ventrum with ethanol.
Pinch and raise the skin with dissecting forceps.
Cut through the body wall muscles just anterior to the genital opening and continue along one side of the midline on the ventral side until reaching the thoracic cavity.
Use blunt-end scissors to avoid damaging organs.
Collect the organs of interest for processing into single-cell suspensions.
Put in a new plate with staining medium.
Disaggregate tumor tissue mechanically with the rough side of a microscope slide.
Filter the disaggregated tissue with a 40 μm strainer.
Wash the filter with staining medium to clean it thoroughly.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 400–600 g for 5 min.
Decant off or aspirate the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend the cells with 1 mL of staining medium on ice (4°C).
Count total single cells using a counting chamber (Burker Camera) or an alternative method (hemocytometer).
Put the counted tumor cells in a microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 400–600 g for 5 minutes.
Perform a fast spin of 10 seconds at maximum speed to recover all tumor cells.
Incubate tumor cells with 100 μL of the mixture antibodies for 1 hour at room temperature in the dark.
Collect blood by intracardiac puncture.
Place collected blood in heparin tubes or EDTA tubes (≈300 μL per tube).
Let the blood stand for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Centrifuge at 400–600 g for 5 minutes to obtain plasma.
Aliquot the plasma into 1.5 mL tubes and store at −20°C or −80°C if long-term storage is required.
Transfer the blood pellet into a 50 mL tube.
Add 4 mL of Milli-Q water per heparin tube.
Gently shake the 50 mL tube up and down on ice for 30 seconds.
Stop the lysis reaction by adding 1× PBS up to 50 mL.
Discard coagulates and then fill up to 50 mL with 1× PBS.
Optionally, add 1 mL of RBC 1× lysis buffer for erythrocyte lysis.
Incubate the sample containing RBC lysis buffer on ice for 3 minutes.
Centrifuge the 50 mL tube at 400–600 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Decant the supernatant carefully without losing the pellet.
Resuspend the pellet with 1 mL of staining medium and transfer to a 1.5 mL tube at 4°C.
Count total single cells, aiming for approximately 300,000–600,000 blood cells per panel.
Incubate blood cells with 100 μL of mixture antibodies for 1 hour at room temperature.
Remove the femur and skin of syngeneic mice.
Cut both epiphyses slightly to facilitate passage of an insulin or a 23G syringe.
Flush 3 mL of staining medium through the femoral shaft to obtain bone marrow cells.
Disaggregate groups of cells stuck together using a pipette.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 400–600 g for 5 min.
Decant or aspirate the supernatant after centrifugation.
Add 900 μL of Milli-Q water to the pellet to lysate erythrocytes.
Gently pipette or shake the mixture up and down for 30 s on ice.
Stop the reaction by adding 100 μL of 10× PBS.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 400–600 g for 5 min.
Decant or aspirate the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend the pellet with 1 mL of staining medium.
Pass the cell suspension through a 40 μm strainer using a plunger from a 50 mL syringe to improve filtration.
Centrifuge the 50 mL tube at 400–600 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the pellet with 1 mL of staining medium on ice.
Count total single cells, aiming for approximately 300,000–600,000 bone marrow cells per panel.
Incubate bone marrow cells with 100 μL of mixture antibodies for 1 hour at room temperature.
Disaggregate spleen tissue mechanically with the rough side of a microscope slide until well disaggregated and the solution appears red and turbid with few aggregates.
Put the disaggregated spleen tissue in a 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 400–600 g for 5 minutes.
Decant off or vacuum the supernatant after centrifugation.
Lose erythrocytes from the cell suspension with 900 μL of Milli-Q water by pipetting up and down almost 5 times to resuspend the pellet.
Optional: Use RBC 1× lysis buffer for erythrocyte lysis by adding 1 mL, letting it sit for 3 minutes on ice, then stopping the reaction with 100 μL of 10× PBS.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 400–600 g for 5 minutes after lysis.
Decant off or vacuum the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend cells with 1 mL of staining medium on ice.
Filter the resuspended cells through a 40 μm strainer placed in a 50 mL tube on ice, using a plunger to improve filtration if necessary.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 400–600 g for 5 minutes after filtering.
Decant off or vacuum the supernatant after centrifugation.
Count total single cells.
Incubate spleen cells with 100 μL of mixture antibodies during 1 h at RT.
Know which lasers are available in your Flow Cytometry Facility's cytometer.
Determine the number of detectors for each laser in your cytometer.
Consider the type of filter in front of each detector to choose fluorochrome combinations.
Choose fluorochromes based on the number and configuration of lasers, detectors, and filters.
Pair highly expressed antigens with dimmer fluorochromes.
Pair lower expression antigens with brighter fluorochromes.
Optimize the panel by titrating antibodies correctly.
Set correct voltages for each detector in the flow cytometer.
Correct for spectral overlap using fluorescence compensation.
Include an unstained sample to correct for autofluorescence inherent to cells.
Select compensation controls that involve single-color antibodies conjugated to the same fluorophores used in the experiment.
Collect compensation controls and experimental samples on the flow cytometer with identical instrument settings.
Generate compensation matrices that describe the spectral overlap between the fluorophores using software.
Apply the generated compensation matrices to the experimental data to correct for spectral overlap.
Optimize the compensation settings to minimize compensation errors and validate the compensation strategy using appropriate positive and negative controls.
Set up Fluorescence Minus One (FMO) controls to properly interpret flow cytometry data.
Prepare a single-cell suspension using the appropriate protocol and adjust the cell amount from 600,000 to 1 million cells in staining medium in each tube.
Centrifuge the single cell suspension at 400–600 g for 5 minutes.
Add the optimized dilution mixture of antibodies to the respective tubes.
Incubate the tubes for 1 hour at room temperature in the dark.
Centrifuge the 1.5 ml tube at 400–600 g for 5 minutes.
Wash the cells once with ice-cold staining medium at 400–600 g for 5 minutes.
Resuspend the cells with 100–200 μL FACS buffer.
Prepare a single cell suspension using a specific protocol depending on the tissue.
Perform the cell membrane staining protocol or cell surface markers.
Centrifuge the 1.5 mL tube at 400–600 g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant and add 100 μL of staining medium to wash the cells.
After the last wash, discard the supernatant.
Pulse vortex the sample to completely dissociate the pellet.
Critical: Obtain a good suspension of individual cells.
Fix the cells by adding 200 μL of Fixation/Permeabilization Buffer at a 1:3 dilution with Fixation/Permeabilization Diluent to each 1.5 mL tube.
Pipette up and down the pellet to homogenize better.
Incubate for 30–60 min at room temperature, protecting from light.
Centrifuge samples at 400–600 g at room temperature for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Add 200 μL of 1× Permeabilization Buffer to each tube.
Centrifuge samples at 400–600 g at room temperature for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Repeat Step 73 (resuspend pellet in residual volume).
Optional: Block with 2% normal mouse/rat serum by adding 2 μL directly to the cells.
Incubate at room temperature for 15 min.
Add the recommended amount of directly conjugated antibody for intracellular antigen detection.
Incubate for at least 30 min at room temperature in the dark.
Centrifuge samples at 400–600 g at room temperature for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Add 200 μL of 1× Permeabilization Buffer to each tube.
Centrifuge samples at 400–600 g at RT for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend stained cells in an appropriate volume of Flow Cytometry Buffer (100–200 μL).
Power on the flow cytometer and the computer that controls it.
Check that the lasers are working correctly and calibrated according to the manufacturer’s specifications.
Set up the appropriate filters and detectors for the fluorophores used in the experiment.
Adjust the gain and voltage settings for the detectors to optimize the signal-to-noise ratio for each fluorescence channel.
Perform a quality control check with calibration beads to ensure the flow cytometer is working correctly.
Run compensation tubes to perform compensation and correct for the spectral overlap.
Prepare the sample and load it into the sample injection port or chamber.
Run the sample through the flow cytometer and collect data.
Analyze the data using appropriate software such as FlowJo 8.7 (FlowJo Software, BD) or BD FACSDiva Software to generate scatter plots and histograms to identify the different cell populations.
Transfer samples to individual FACS tubes.
Set the voltages of FSC-A and SSC-A plot using unstained control depending on cell type.
Draw a gate around all cell events in the FSC-A and SSC-A plot.
In the FSC-A and FSC-H plot, draw a gate around the diagonal to select only single cells.
Draw dot plots showing different fluorochrome combinations based on each immune panel.
Use FMO controls to set proper gates in each dot plot.
Once spread has been identified, set the gate correctly to show real positivity/negativity for a given marker.
Acquire all samples and ensure that record at least 10,000 events of your selected population.
Perform the acquisition of the stained tubes using the BD FACSCanto II flow cytometer.
Export data according to your institute’s core facility guidelines.
